bib.title: ChatGPT outperforms crowd-workers for text-annotation tasks
bib.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

question: Can zero-shot ChatGPT match or beat MTurk crowd-workers (and trained annotators on agreement) for text-annotation tasks, and at what cost?
contributions: First systematic evaluation of ChatGPT zero-shot for text annotation across relevance, stance, topic and frame tasks
Comparison of accuracy and intercoder agreement against MTurk and trained annotators, plus per-annotation cost

method.summary: Same codebooks given to three trained annotators, MTurk Masters and gpt-3.5-turbo (zero-shot, one chat session per tweet). Accuracy is agreement with trained-annotator gold labels; intercoder agreement is percent same label between two annotators or two ChatGPT runs.
method.task: text annotation: relevance, stance, topic, problem/solution frames, 14 policy frames

datasets.name: Content moderation tweets Jan 2023
datasets.source: new sample, to address memorization concern

inference.samples: 2 responses per tweet per temperature, 4 per tweet in total; new chat session per tweet
inference.prompting: Zero-shot, codebook instruction text identical to MTurk; tweets fed one by one with 'Here's the tweet I picked, please label it as [Task Specific Instruction]'; no ChatGPT-specific prompting

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.definition: correctly classified instances over total, trained annotations as gold, only texts both trained annotators agreed on

metrics.name: Intercoder agreement
metrics.definition: percent of instances where both annotators in a group (or two ChatGPT runs) report the same class

baselines: MTurk crowd-workers (Masters, US, approval >90% with >=50 approved HITs, max 20% of tweets per worker, 2 workers per tweet)
eval.protocol: No significance tests stated; Pearson correlations across tasks reported

prompts.text: Here’s the tweet I picked, please label it as [Task Specific Instruction (e.g. ‘one of the topics in the instruction’)].

results.claim: ChatGPT zero-shot accuracy exceeds MTurk by about 25 points on average
results.setup: Four datasets (n=6,183), gpt-3.5-turbo zero-shot, MTurk Masters in US, trained annotators as gold standard
results.quote: On average, ChatGPT’s accuracy exceeds that of MTurk by about 25 percentage points.

results.setup: Four datasets (n=6,183), gpt-3.5-turbo zero-shot, MTurk Masters in US, trained annotators as gold standard
results.quote: intercoder agreement is about 56% for MTurk, 79% for trained annotators, 91% for ChatGPT with temperature = 1, and 97% for ChatGPT with temperature = 0.2

results.claim: Mean intercoder agreement for trained annotators
results.setup: Four datasets (n=6,183), gpt-3.5-turbo zero-shot, MTurk Masters in US, trained annotators as gold standard
results.quote: intercoder agreement is about 56% for MTurk, 79% for trained annotators, 91% for ChatGPT with temperature = 1, and 97% for ChatGPT with temperature = 0.2

results.quote: intercoder agreement is about 56% for MTurk, 79% for trained annotators, 91% for ChatGPT with temperature = 1, and 97% for ChatGPT with temperature = 0.2

results.setup: Four datasets (n=6,183), gpt-3.5-turbo zero-shot, MTurk Masters in US, trained annotators as gold standard
results.quote: intercoder agreement is about 56% for MTurk, 79% for trained annotators, 91% for ChatGPT with temperature = 1, and 97% for ChatGPT with temperature = 0.2

results.claim: ChatGPT cost per annotation under $0.003, about thirty times cheaper than MTurk
results.quote: the per-annotation cost of ChatGPT is less than $0.003—about thirty times cheaper than MTurk

results.claim: Correlation between intercoder agreement and accuracy is positive but weak
results.setup: Four datasets (n=6,183), gpt-3.5-turbo zero-shot, MTurk Masters in US, trained annotators as gold standard
results.quote: The correlation between intercoder agreement and accuracy is positive (Pearson’s r = 0.36).

results.claim: ChatGPT accuracy correlates with trained-annotator agreement (easier tasks better)
results.setup: Four datasets (n=6,183), gpt-3.5-turbo zero-shot, MTurk Masters in US, trained annotators as gold standard
results.quote: ChatGPT’s accuracy is positively correlated with the intercoder agreement of trained annotators (Pearson’s r = 0.46)

results.claim: ChatGPT outperformance of MTurk correlates negatively with trained-annotator agreement (bigger gain on harder tasks)

limits: Gold standard is trained annotators (research assistants), and accuracy counts only texts both agreed on
Per-task accuracy values are only in Figure 1, text prints just the relevance accuracies
Only gpt-3.5-turbo, English-focused, zero-shot, one topic area (content moderation) plus Congress tweets
Authors say further research needed: multilingual, few-shot, chain of thought, other LLMs
Relevance 2023 accuracy only 59%, prompt lacked examples
Outperformance claimed vs MTurk, not vs trained annotators on accuracy
